chunks: And Sulaymān ibn Khālid narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
Indeed, I dislike renting the millstone by itself and then leasing it out for more than what I rented it for, unless I make some alteration in it or incur some expense in it.

key_terms.أُؤَاجِرَهَا: to lease it out to another
key_terms.أُحْدِثَ: to make a change or improvement

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to rent an item and then lease it out for a higher price in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a fiqh ruling related to leasing and subleasing property for profit. It indicates dislike for renting an item and then leasing it for a higher amount without adding value or bearing expense, highlighting fairness in economic dealings.
